searches.note: Twenty one searches of twenty eight, seven unspent. Most searches blocked the author's own domains so the second source would be independent; four were held to a house's own domain to read its sheets. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: founding, people and dates, grapes, sites, making, label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail stood in one source or none it was cut or hedged.

Austen and Napoleon (Wikipedia, the novel's summaries, Decanter); the tariff of 1861 and phylloxera (Wikipedia, GuildSomm, a Cambridge review). Austen line changed; the rest sound.

codexTension: The region summary and the library record of Klein Constantia say Klein Constantia is a portion of the 1685 estate; true of the land, but Wikipedia, Wine With Seth and Wine Spectator date its making as a separate farm to the early nineteenth century, not to the division of 1712. Reported, not edited.
The library's 'Constantia was the first non-European wine to hold European fame' is a claim of a first not tested here. Reported, not edited.
